subject: FinBotics technical alignment — SDK/auth, reranker path & capacity proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finbotics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call notes + info needed for dedicated capacity proposal

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and explicit asks so we can size a clean Dedicated proposal and an integration runbook for your POC.

High-level summary (we covered):
- Goal: Replace FinBotics' inference tier for question-answering and a lightweight reranker for search with Redwood Dedicated (VPC).
- Primary flows: 1) streaming chat/generation (tool-calls for doc lookup), and 2) embed + rerank (batched).
- Security constraints: SSO + SCIM, strict audit log retention (12 months), and egress policy to your VPC.

What we need from you (please answer inline):
1) Traffic profile: steady qps during business hours, expected peak spikes. Can you provide avg tokens/request and peak requests per minute? (you mentioned ~200 qps steady, confirm).
2) Latency SLO: P95 target for chat generation and for reranker endpoints.
3) Retry tolerances — is 2 retries acceptable for short transient errors?
4) Preferred auth: OAuth service account + mTLS, or API key scoped to VPC? Any corporate procurement constraints?
5) Embedding pattern: will embeddings be computed upstream and uploaded, or do you expect Redwood to compute embeddings on ingest?

Proposed next steps from our side:
- We’ll draft a minimal topology proposal (warm pool + autoscale bursts) and an ops sprint plan to validate auth/SDK integration in your staging.
- Deliver a cost/throughput estimate for 200 qps steady / 1,000 qps burst and a POC schedule.

Attachments: placeholder for your requirement spreadsheet if you want to attach (I’ll drop our topology proposal in the next mail).

Thanks — Karthik

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call notes + info needed for dedicated capacity proposal

Karthik / team — thanks for the recap. Answers inline below and attached our POC requirements workbook.

1) Traffic: steady ~200 qps (business hrs), typical payload 120–220 tokens per request. Peak events up to ~1,000 qps for short windows (1–10 minutes) during batch runs.
2) Latency SLO: P95 < 350ms for short completions (<256 tokens). For reranker endpoints P95 < 150ms.
3) Retries: yes, 1–2 retries acceptable as long as retries are visible in audit logs.
4) Auth: Security pref is OAuth2 service account integrated with our IdP (Okta). mTLS for inter-node is a plus but not required for POC. Procurement prefers scoped service identities over long-lived API keys.
5) Embeddings: we will compute embeddings in our ingestion pipeline and push vectors to your embeddings endpoint for storage/retrieval. Reranker will call embeddings + model endpoint.

Attachment: FinBotics_POC_requirements.xlsx (workbook with traffic curves, dataset sizes, and compliance checklist).

Also — our security team flagged SOC 2 type II evidence and detailed audit logs (per-token request IDs). They requested a sample audit log format and retention policy. Procurement will follow up to lock down NDA/PO terms.

—Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed topology + autoscale sketch (attached)

Alex — attaching the initial topology JSON and a short ops sketch. High-level proposal below so the team can review quickly.

Topology summary (POC):
- Dedicated pool in your VPC (single region, us-east-1) with 3-tier node groups:
  1) Warm pool (min 4 GPUs): keeps model weights resident, KV cache priming for common prompts.
  2) Steady worker pool (based on throughput): sized for 200 qps steady assuming 120 tokens/request; we estimate 10 A100 equivalent GPUs (logical) — will refine after load tests.
  3) Burst autoscale group: rapid scale out to handle short peaks up to 1,000 qps — leverage pre-warmed images and incremental kernel hotstart.

Queues & concurrency model:
- Per-route queues: separate queues for "chat/generation" and "embed+rerank" to isolate latency budgets.
- Concurrency cap per instance: configurable 16 concurrent streams for generation (depends on model/quant).
- Rate shaping: token-bucket at the ingress gateway to protect steady pool; burst tokens consumed from warm pool first.

Auth & SDK integration:
- Recommend OAuth2 service account for API tokens + short-lived scoped JWTs for per-route enforcement.
- SDK: we’ll provide a small Node + Python SDK snippet for token exchange (Okta SSO flow) and a sample middleware to attach request metadata for audit logs (request_id, user_id, route).

Structured output & tool-calling notes:
- Tool-calling: we’ll surface the tool-calling API via a lightweight webhook connector that can be called from the runtime (signed webhook requests).
- Structured output: support JSON-schema hints in prompts + a verification pass on the server to ensure schema conformity before returning final payload (will add validation errors to structured response).

Embeddings & reranker path:
- You compute embeddings upstream. For reranking we recommend a two-stage path: 1) dense retrieval using your vector DB (you already have), 2) N-best rerank using a low-latency model on Redwood (per-route queue).
- Batch sizes for rerankers: prefer micro-batches of 8–32 to preserve latency SLO while improving throughput.

Compliance & logs:
- We can provide sample audit logs (per-request JSON lines) and retention policy controls (12/24/36 months). Will attach sample log schema in follow-up.

Costs: rough order-of-magnitude estimate in attachment for 200 qps steady / 1,000 qps burst. This is ballpark — final pricing after runbook and sizing tests.

Next steps:
- Review the attached topology JSON and comment on pool sizes and auth preference.
- We propose a two-week POC: week 1 = SDK/auth + smoke tests; week 2 = load tests and reranker integration.
- Schedule alignment call for Monday May 24th to lock the POC cadence.

Attachment: redwood-proposed-topology.json (small topology sketch).

Thanks — Karthik

(Attachment: redwood-proposed-topology.json (json, 8 KB))

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed topology + autoscale sketch (questions)

Thanks Karthik — couple quick clarifications from ops/embeddings perspective:

1) Warm pool behavior: how long do we keep KV cache entries for active sessions? Suggest TTL = 15 minutes for chat sessions and longer for background warmed prefixes. This affects memory retention and costs.
2) Burst cold-start: for the burst autoscale we plan incremental kernel hotstart — confirm whether pre-warmed ARM images are required for your environment or if using AMI with init hooks is sufficient.
3) Reranker batch sizing: given FinBotics' P95 target (150ms) we should prioritize micro-batches <= 16 and ensure the reranker pool has lower concurrency (4–8 per instance). Alex — please confirm if your vector DB can return candidate sets in <40ms so we can budget reranker latency.
4) Tool-calling webhook: we need to limit outbound webhook concurrency and add a retry/backoff policy. Also propose an optional sandbox mode that signs payloads with a short-lived key so your endpoints can verify provenance.

I'll capture these and update the topology JSON after we hear back on the vector DB latency and the IdP auth flow.

—Soojin
